facts.claim: Only one shape is repaired: a single open-ended entry whose text opens with the old-text key, has exactly one separator to the new-text key, and ends with that key's string value and no closing bracket; anything more is refused.
facts.catch_criteria: States the narrow accepted shape (one entry, one separator, open-ended tail) and that other mixed shapes are refused.

facts.claim: The new text is read as a JSON string; a tail that is not one closed JSON string is refused.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the new text is JSON-parsed and that an unparseable tail is refused.

facts.claim: The old text is kept raw, not decoded: an escape such as backslash-n stays two characters.
facts.catch_criteria: Contrasts the raw old text with the JSON-decoded new text.

facts.claim: Dispatch coerces the call before validation, and execution reads the coerced list, so an accepted mixed call executes as a normal edit.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the coercion happens at dispatch before validation and that the edit executes the coerced entries.

facts.claim: The streaming validator and the diff preview read the edits list only as JSON text, so they see no entry for a mixed call that the tool applies.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the preview or streaming validator does not see the repaired entry of a mixed call.

traps.wrong_answer: Every edit call written in mixed syntax is repaired and applied.
The streaming preview shows the same replacement that the tool applies.
Old and new texts are both JSON-decoded, so an escaped newline in the old text matches a real newline.
